_comment: Grants reported on grantmaking.ai that Trace does not already hold from the original source. The site largely restates Manifund, EA Funds, SFF and Coefficient Giving — 94% of its rows match grants Trace ingests directly, so only the remainder is here. Most of what is left is grantee-reported funding from outside the EA ecosystem (NSF, NSERC, UNDP, the EU, AWS, Emergent Ventures). Grants are self-reported by grantees and unverified; amounts the grantee chose not to publish are null. Recipients resolve to the project’s organisation where it has one, otherwise the person leading it, because a project title is a description rather than a counterparty. Refreshing means re-reading every project page: the grants are rendered into the page, not served by the API, so there is no incremental feed. Snapshot taken 2026-08-27 across 1,719 projects.

We host monthly AI Safety dialogues for African talent, bringing these conversations directly to the community. In the final week of each month, we run small “AI Safety Action Weeks” focused on a specific theme, designed for the African diaspora. Each action week includes three Friday evening sessions and weekend keynotes, along with short, hands-on quests that participants complete to demonstrate engagement. These might include applying to a BlueDot course, summarizing an AI Safety paper, re-running well-known ML algorithms, amplifying a campaign, or building something at a hackathon. Our theory of change is that by anchoring these conversations within the African context, we can help students build a tangible presence in the AI Safety space and increase participation through targeted, incentive-driven engagement.

Phase 1 was funded by a $650 BlueDot Impact Rapid Grant; the deliverables below are public. The estimator recovers known ground-truth effects on a synthetic testbed (all three 95% credible intervals contain the truth) - a pre-registered go/no-go gate, cleared before any real-model spend. The rho* frontier separates a genuinely causal case (rho* = 0.69) from a decorative baseline (rho* = 0.05). In real planted-hint audits of an open model (Llama-3.1-8B, up to n = 103 per run, free-tier inference), 36.9% of runs followed the planted hint, mostly without acknowledging it in the CoT - and the auditor flagged them (verdicts still heuristic until the golden set below validates them). A real caught transcript is public. MIT-licensed repo with a 124-test CI suite: https://github.com/thylinao1/bayes-cot-faithfulness - interactive demo and evidence: https://thylinao1.github.io/bayes-cot-faithfulness/site/
